title: Feature request: allow `initial` in workflow_map() to take as input an entire `workflow set` object
description:
A great feature of the `tune_bayes()` and `tune_sim_anneal()` is the `initial` argument that can be the output from a previous `tune_grid()` call. 

Unfortunately, this feature becomes quite cumbersome for `workflow_set`  objects? This stack [post](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/79520521/r-tidymodels-how-to-pass-argument-initial-using-workflow-map) shows that passing `workflow_map(initial =tune_grid)` won't work, and the suggested answer is a rather verbose and manual recursive call:

```
workflow_set() %>% 
 ## add for one model
  option_add(
    id = "recipe_lasso",
    initial = tune_grid_res %>% extract_workflow_set_result("recipe_lasso")
  ) %>% 
  ## repeat for every model....
  option_add(..) %>% 
  option_add(..) %>% 
  workflow_map()

```

this is also slightly counter-intuitive, as the `option_add()` is added to the initial `workflow_set`, not to the `workflow_map()` call?

Would it be possible to have an explicit argument `initial` in `workflow_map()` that would possibly take as input a previous `workflow_set` and.... map it to the underlying modelling function?

Thanks!

Below is an example, together with a manual solution function `option_add_initial()` which is quite... untidy!


``` r
library(tidymodels)

# Load and prepare data
ames_data <- ames[,sapply(ames, class) %in% c("integer", "numeric")]

# Define a recipe
recipe <- recipe(Sale_Price ~ ., data = ames_data) %>%
  step_normalize(all_predictors())

# Define models
lasso_model <- linear_reg(penalty = tune(), mixture = 1) %>%
  set_engine("glmnet")

rf_model <- rand_forest(min_n = tune(), trees = 100) %>%
  set_engine("ranger") %>%
  set_mode("regression")

# Create workflows
lasso_wf <- workflow() %>%
  add_model(lasso_model) %>%
  add_recipe(recipe)

rf_wf <- workflow() %>%
  add_model(rf_model) %>%
  add_recipe(recipe)

cross_val <- vfold_cv(ames_data, v = 5)

tune_grid_res <- 
  workflow_set(
    preproc = list(recipe),
    models = list(lasso = lasso_model, rf = rf_model)) %>%
  workflow_map("tune_grid", resamples = cross_val, grid = 10)


option_add_initial <- function(workflow_set, workflow_with_grid_results){

  res <- workflow_set
  for(i in 1:nrow(workflow_with_grid_results)){
    id_i <- workflow_with_grid_results$wflow_id[[i]]
    res <- res %>% 
      option_add(
        id = id_i,
        initial = workflow_with_grid_results %>% extract_workflow_set_result(id_i)
      ) 
  }
  res
}

tune_bayes_res <- workflow_set(
  preproc = list(recipe),
  models = list(lasso = lasso_model, rf = rf_model)
  ) %>% 
  option_add_initial(workflow_with_grid_results = tune_grid_res) %>%

title: Why is "preproc" designated by the type rather than the name of the preprocessor?
description:
Perhaps I'm missing something obvious, but why is the `preproc` field in the `info` column populated with the preprocessor _type_ rather than the name, as passed in when calling `workflow_set`?

My expectation would have been that `autoplot` would distinguish between different preprocessors using shape, but that appears to only happen if they are passed in as different types:

```
library(workflowsets)
library(workflows)
library(modeldata)
library(recipes)
library(parsnip)
library(dplyr)
library(rsample)
library(tune)
library(yardstick)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

data(two_class_dat, package = "modeldata")

set.seed(1)
folds <- vfold_cv(two_class_dat, v = 5)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

decision_tree_rpart_spec <-
  decision_tree(min_n = tune(), cost_complexity = tune()) |>
  set_engine('rpart') |>
  set_mode('classification')

logistic_reg_glm_spec <-
  logistic_reg() |>
  set_engine('glm')

mars_earth_spec <-
  mars(prod_degree = tune()) |>
  set_engine('earth') |>
  set_mode('classification')

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def_recipe <- 
  recipe(Class ~ A + B,data = two_class_dat)

yj_recipe <-
  recipe(Class ~ ., data = two_class_dat) |>
  step_YeoJohnson(A, B)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

two_class_set1 <-
  workflow_set(
    preproc = list(none = Class ~ A + B, yj_trans = yj_recipe),
    models = list(cart = decision_tree_rpart_spec, glm = logistic_reg_glm_spec,
                  mars = mars_earth_spec)
  )

two_class_set2 <-
  workflow_set(
    preproc = list(none = def_recipe, yj_trans = yj_recipe),
    models = list(cart = decision_tree_rpart_spec, glm = logistic_reg_glm_spec,
                  mars = mars_earth_spec)
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

two_class_res1 <-
  two_class_set1 |>
  workflow_map(
    resamples = folds,
    grid = 10,
    seed = 2,
    verbose = TRUE,
    control = control_grid(save_workflow = TRUE)
  )

two_class_res2 <-
  two_class_set2 |>
  workflow_map(
    resamples = folds,
    grid = 10,
    seed = 2,
    verbose = TRUE,
    control = control_grid(save_workflow = TRUE)
  )

# Uses shape for the two different preprocessors
autoplot(two_class_res1)

# All preprocessors are simply "recipe" and you can't tell them apart
autoplot(two_class_res2)
```

title: collect_extracts() for workflow_set
description:
I noticed that workflowsets does not appear to have a method for collecting extracts and it has a method for collecting notes https://github.com/tidymodels/workflowsets/issues/135.

> class(results)
[1] "workflow_set" "tbl_df"       "tbl"          "data.frame"
> collect_extracts(results)
Error in `collect_extracts()`:
! No `collect_extracts()` exists for a <workflow_set/tbl_df/tbl/data.frame> object.
Run `rlang::last_trace()` to see where the error occurred.

It would be handy to have collect_extracts implemented so that you can get elapsed time or other information extracted.

Here one example using partials if you want to reuse the code for mulitple collect_*

```{r}
my_collect_custom <- function(wflow_set_results, fn){
  wflow_set_rsl <- wflow_set_results %>%
    dplyr::select(wflow_id, result)
  
  distinct_list_of_workflows <- wflow_set_rsl %>%
    dplyr::select(wflow_id) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    pull(wflow_id)
  
  collect_fn_helper <- function(x){
    wflow_set_rsl %>%
          filter(wflow_id == x) %>%
          pull(result) %>%
          pluck(1) %>%
          fn()
  }
  list_dfs <- map_dfr(
    set_names(distinct_list_of_workflows),
    collect_fn_helper,
    .id = "workflow_id")
  
  list_dfs
}

my_collect_extracts <- purrr::partial(my_collect_custom, fn = collect_extracts)
my_collect_extracts(results)

my_collect_notes <- purrr::partial(my_collect_custom, fn = collect_notes)
my_collect_notes(results)

```

description:
`workflowsets:::check_tune_args` doesn't allow passing `eval_time` as an argument, which means that censored regression models can't be evaluated with the package:

``` r
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tidymodels))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(censored))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(baguette))

set.seed(1)
sim_dat <- prodlim::SimSurv(500) %>%
  mutate(event_time = Surv(time, event)) %>%
  select(event_time, X1, X2)

set.seed(2)
split <- initial_split(sim_dat)
sim_tr <- training(split)
sim_te <- testing(split)
sim_rs <- vfold_cv(sim_tr)

time_points <- c(10, 1, 5, 15)

spec_bt <-
  bag_tree() %>%
  set_mode("censored regression")

spec_ph <-
  proportional_hazards(penalty = .5) %>%
  set_engine("glmnet") %>%
  set_mode("censored regression")

wflow_set <-
  workflow_set(
    preproc = list(form = event_time ~ X1 + X2),
    models = list(bt = spec_bt, ph = spec_ph)
  )


wflow_set_fit_stc <-
  workflow_map(
    wflow_set,
    "fit_resamples",
    seed = 2193,
    resamples = sim_rs,
    metrics = metric_set(brier_survival_integrated),
    eval_time = time_points
  )
#> Error in `halt()`:
#> ! The following options cannot be used as arguments for `fit_resamples()` or the `tune_*()` functions: 'eval_time'
#> Execution stopped; returning current results
```

title: Predict on new_data from a workflow_set
description:
## Feature

Once a set of `workflow`s in a `workflow_set` have been fitted, e.g. by `workflow_map()`, it would be nice to be able to `predict()` from these `workflow`s to `new_data`s. Currently I'm not sure how to do this, tell me if I'm missing an obvious solution.

I would suggest using `lm_models %>% workflow_map("predict", new_data = ames_test)`, see below.

## Reprex

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)

# get train, test, folds object
ames_split <- initial_split(ames, prop = 0.80)
ames_train <- training(ames_split)
ames_test  <-  testing(ames_split)
ames_folds <- vfold_cv(ames_train, v = 10)

basic_rec <- 
  recipe(Sale_Price ~ Neighborhood + Gr_Liv_Area + Year_Built + Bldg_Type + 
           Latitude + Longitude, data = ames_train) %>%
  step_log(Gr_Liv_Area, base = 10) %>% 
  step_other(Neighborhood, threshold = 0.01) %>% 
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors())

interaction_rec <-

description:
Hi tidymodels team,
I've found myself wanting to extract the `param_info` `parameter` sets from a `workflow_set` to compare the ranges tested with those selected as the best performing parameters after tuning to check if the best performing parameters happened to be at/near the extreme of the range tested, thus justifying an expansion of the range in the direction suggested by the extreme.

I thought about naming it `pull_param_info` but opted for a `parameters` method instead. I'm not sure which makes the most sense. 

Would this be useful to add to `workflowsets` or `dials`?

```r
library(tidymodels)
data(concrete, package = "modeldata")
glimpse(concrete)
concrete <- 
  concrete %>% 
  group_by(cement, blast_furnace_slag, fly_ash, water, superplasticizer, 
           coarse_aggregate, fine_aggregate, age) %>% 
  summarize(compressive_strength = mean(compressive_strength),
            .groups = "drop")
nrow(concrete)
set.seed(1501)
concrete_split <- initial_split(concrete, strata = compressive_strength)
concrete_train <- training(concrete_split)
concrete_test  <- testing(concrete_split)

set.seed(1502)
concrete_folds <- 
  vfold_cv(concrete_train, strata = compressive_strength, repeats = 5)

normalized_rec <- 
  recipe(compressive_strength ~ ., data = concrete_train) %>% 
  step_normalize(all_predictors()) 

nnet_spec <- 
  mlp(hidden_units = tune(), penalty = tune(), epochs = tune()) %>% 
  set_engine("nnet", MaxNWts = 2600) %>% 
  set_mode("regression")

svm_r_spec <- 
  svm_rbf(cost = tune(), rbf_sigma = tune()) %>% 
  set_engine("kernlab") %>% 
  set_mode("regression")

svm_p_spec <- 
  svm_poly(cost = tune(), degree = tune()) %>% 
  set_engine("kernlab") %>% 
  set_mode("regression")

knn_spec <- 
  nearest_neighbor(neighbors = tune(), dist_power = tune(), weight_func = tune()) %>% 
  set_engine("kknn") %>% 
  set_mode("regression")

nnet_param <- 
  nnet_spec %>% 
  parameters() %>% 
  update(hidden_units = hidden_units(c(1, 27)))

normalized <- 
  workflowsets::workflow_set(
    preproc = list(normalized = normalized_rec), 
    models = list(SVM_radial = svm_r_spec, SVM_poly = svm_p_spec, 
                  KNN = knn_spec, neural_network = nnet_spec)
  )
  

 has_param_info <- function(x) {
  any(grepl("param", purrr::flatten_chr(purrr::map(x$option, names))))
}

#'@export
parameters.workflow_set <- function(x, id) {
  
  if (!missing(id)) {
    y <- x %>% dplyr::filter(wflow_id %in% id)
    if (nrow(y) < 1) 
      halt("No workflow found with ID(s) ",paste0(id, collapse = ","))
  } else
    y <- x
  
  if (has_param_info(y)) {
    out <- purrr::map(y$option, ~{
      .out <- .x[grepl("param", names(.x))]
      if (!rlang::is_empty(.out)) .out[[1]]
    })
  } else
    out <- NULL

  if (!missing(id))
    if (length(id) == 1) out <- out[[1]]
  out
}



normalized %>% 
  workflowsets::option_add(param = nnet_param, id = "normalized_neural_network") %>% 
  parameters.workflow_set()
 
```

title: Tune bayes ignores random forest in workflow_map
description:
I'm having a problem with the `workflow_map()` function. I have created a set of models and preprocessing using the `workflow_set` function. 

I am not able to run my random forest model using workflow_map and tune_bayes.

I have a feeling that this is to do with mtry not being specified, however, I have tried specifying this using `option_add()` or `param_info()` inside the `workflow_map` call. 

Interestingly this problem doesn't occur when using control grid, which says it is "Creating pre-processing data to finalize unknown parameter: mtry" when it is run. 

```r
rf_model <- rand_forest(mtry = tune(),
                        trees = tune(),
                        min_n = tune()) %>%
  set_engine("ranger", importance = "impurity") %>%
  set_mode("regression") %>%
  parsnip::translate()

all_workflows <- workflowsets::workflow_set(preproc = list(tree_rec),
                              models = list(random_forest = rf_model)) %>%
  option_add(param = rf_params, id = "recipe_random_forest")

bayes_ctrl <- tune::control_bayes(save_pred = TRUE,
                                  verbose = TRUE,
                                  no_improve = 1,
                                  seed=seed,
                                  parallel_over = "everything",
                                  save_workflow = TRUE)
# This does not run the model correctly

results <- all_workflows %>% 
  workflow_map(seed = seed,
               fn = "tune_bayes",
               resamples = cv,
               control = bayes_ctrl)

# This method seems to work

grid_ctrl <-
   control_grid(
      save_pred = TRUE,
      parallel_over = "everything",
      save_workflow = TRUE
   )

grid_results <-
   all_workflows %>%
   workflow_map(
      seed = seed,
      resamples = cv,
      grid = 25,
      control = grid_ctrl
   )
```

Thanks in advance!

title: Options in workflowsets - Adding multiple parameter sets & unnamed options
description:
Hi tidymodels team,
Below are some issues I encountered while exploring workflowsets with the R4DS TMWR bookclub Cohort 2. Hope they're helpful to know!

1. Multiple parameter sets can be added if they are named differently. (Possibly a problem, though it could be by design. )
2. If unnamed options already exist, new options can't be added because the error `"All options must be named"` will be triggered when using `option_add`. Unfortunately, I can't remember how I managed to add unnamed options to the `workflow_set` 🤷! If I am able to reproduce it again, I'll add demo code here. Here is an image of the options output for the `workflow_set` that I somehow managed to add the blank options too.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/32208821/119357794-f73b8280-bc75-11eb-9d46-fe17db3cfdce.png)


Here's some code from TMWR to demonstrate.
```r
library(tidymodels)
data(concrete, package = "modeldata")
glimpse(concrete)
concrete <- 
  concrete %>% 
  group_by(cement, blast_furnace_slag, fly_ash, water, superplasticizer, 
           coarse_aggregate, fine_aggregate, age) %>% 
  summarize(compressive_strength = mean(compressive_strength),
            .groups = "drop")
nrow(concrete)
set.seed(1501)
concrete_split <- initial_split(concrete, strata = compressive_strength)
concrete_train <- training(concrete_split)
concrete_test  <- testing(concrete_split)

set.seed(1502)
concrete_folds <- 
  vfold_cv(concrete_train, strata = compressive_strength, repeats = 5)

normalized_rec <- 
  recipe(compressive_strength ~ ., data = concrete_train) %>% 
  step_normalize(all_predictors()) 

nnet_spec <- 
  mlp(hidden_units = tune(), penalty = tune(), epochs = tune()) %>% 
  set_engine("nnet", MaxNWts = 2600) %>% 
  set_mode("regression")

svm_r_spec <- 
  svm_rbf(cost = tune(), rbf_sigma = tune()) %>% 
  set_engine("kernlab") %>% 
  set_mode("regression")

svm_p_spec <- 
  svm_poly(cost = tune(), degree = tune()) %>% 
  set_engine("kernlab") %>% 
  set_mode("regression")

knn_spec <- 
  nearest_neighbor(neighbors = tune(), dist_power = tune(), weight_func = tune()) %>% 
  set_engine("kknn") %>% 
  set_mode("regression")

nnet_param <- 
  nnet_spec %>% 
  parameters() %>% 
  update(hidden_units = hidden_units(c(1, 27)))

normalized <- 
  workflowsets::workflow_set(
    preproc = list(normalized = normalized_rec), 
    models = list(SVM_radial = svm_r_spec, SVM_poly = svm_p_spec, 
                  KNN = knn_spec, neural_network = nnet_spec)
  )
```
This demonstrates how it's possible to add parameter sets by different names:
```r
normalized %>% 
  workflowsets::option_add_parameters() %>% 
  workflowsets::option_add(param = nnet_param, id = "normalized_neural_network") %>% 
  workflowsets::option_add(parameters = nnet_param, id = "normalized_neural_network")
  `[[`("option") %>% 
  `[[`(4)
```
How is `workflow_map` actually applying the parameter sets during the tuning process? Will it just use `param_info` since that matches the argument name to `tuning_grid`?
Should `option_add` & `option_add_parameters` check to see if there's a `param` object among the existing options and warn?
To update the parameters, should the named parameter list in options be overwritten by passing a new `param` object to `option_add` with an identical name to the existing `param` object?

title: Different tune grid for each item in the workflow set
description:
I suggest an option to have a custom tune grid for each element in the workflow set (recipe + model spec pair). In other words, an element in the workflow set can be defined by the recipe, model spec & tune grid.

My reasoning is that this could serve two purposes
1. Being able to specify a custom grid for each recipe model spec pair.
2. Since, some models have many tuning parameters, while others might have only 1 or 2 tuning parameters, I might want to use a large grid for the first former, and a smaller grid for the later.

I am not sure if this makes good sense or not.

Hany
```

title: Create the get_best_wf() and wfs_evaluate() functions
description:
Hi!! Thank you very much for developing this package, great job.

Sorry, I made a pull request #42  before submitting a problem.

It occurred to me to create the **get_best_wf()** and **wfs_evaluate()** functions, to complement the final workflow of workflowsets. **get_best_wf()** allows you to select a top number of workflows (or a specific group of workflows) from the output of the **workflow_map()** function.

The workflows are stored in a tibble where the finished workflows are stored with the hyperparameters of recipes or / and of models, the workflow fitted on the train partition and the evaluation metrics on the train and test partitions.

wfs_evaluate() allows obtaining a list with 2 elements, "metrics_cv_test" that saves the evaluation of the metrics in train and test. "fit_models" that protects the workflows fitted on the train partition.

these functions are seen as viable within the scope of workflow sets ?

title: api for creating results
description:
Right now, there are S3 methods for common `tune` functions. This is easy to use but looks really weird since we are chaining together functions that we would not otherwise. 

For example: 

```r
cell_models <-
   cell_models  %>%
   tune_grid(resamples = val_set, grid = 10) %>%
   fit_resamples(resamples = val_set)
```

A better api is needed, perhaps one that (under the hood) does the same as the code above. For example, it might be helpful to use the `map_*()` concept. 

A _bad_ example would be: 

```r
cell_models <-
   cell_models  %>%
   map_fn("tune_grid", resamples = val_set, grid = 10) %>%
   map_fn("fit_resamples", resamples = val_set)
```

perf_data <-
   collect_metrics(chi_models, summarize = FALSE) %>%
   select(wflow_id, .config, id, .estimate) %>%
   mutate(group = paste(wflow_id, .config, sep = "__")) %>%
   inner_join(
      rank_results(chi_models) %>% select(wflow_id, .config, rank),
      by = c("wflow_id", ".config")
   )

groups <-
   perf_data %>%
   distinct(group, rank) %>%
   arrange(rank)

lvls <- groups %>% pluck("group")

perf_data$group <- factor(perf_data$group, levels = lvls)
groups$group <- factor(groups$group, levels = lvls)

best_lvl <- as.character(lvls[1])

``` r

perf_model <- brm(.estimate ~ group + (1 | id), data = perf_data,
                  iter = 5000, chains = 10, cores = 10, seed = 12,
                  refresh = 0)

posteriors <- posterior_samples(perf_model, pars = "^b_")
colnames(posteriors) <- gsub("b_group", "", colnames(posteriors))

   inner_join(groups, by = "group")

   geom_line() +
   ylab("Probability of Being Better")
